terms.definition: The law that energy is never created or destroyed, only changed in form.
terms.function: Keeps the total constant while forms swap.
terms.whereItIs: The flat total line above the readout stack.
terms.whyItMatters: Physics' master ledger — every energy question is 'which form, where did it go?'

terms.definition: The shapes energy takes: kinetic, potential, thermal, light, sound, chemical.
terms.whyItMatters: The same joule can live in a moving cart, a warm rail, or a raised block.
terms.whereItIs: The three live bars of the readout.

terms.definition: The thermal share energy slides into when motion rubs against a surface.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the most common 'missing' energy — conservation says it never vanished, it warmed something.
terms.whereItIs: The small warm-grey slice of the stack.

terms.definition: A system where no energy enters or leaves — the total is constant.
terms.whyItMatters: The frame in which the law holds exactly and tracking forms is simplest.
terms.whereItIs: The coaster rig considered alone on the model.
